findings.title: Owned operations accept pages the OS did not lock
findings.reproduction: Compare WorkArea::new with WorkArea::locked and follow both result and scratch allocation paths.
findings.expected: Before placing any secret, enforce the caller's required OS protections for every allocation.
findings.observed: WorkArea::new can succeed with a false lock status. Flags for a result do not attest earlier scratch allocations. Dump and fork exclusion are separate capabilities.
findings.impact: A successful native encode or recovery can use pageable secret memory. No swap or dump disclosure was measured.
findings.recommendedFix: Introduce one fallible strict allocation policy for all owned results and scratch. Specify required capabilities per OS and reject the operation before secret bytes enter an inadequate region.
findings.requiredVerification: Normal allocation and policy-refusal tests for result and scratch on each supported platform; no partial output on refusal.

findings.title: Portable and caller-owned entry points have no secret-memory boundary
findings.reproduction: Compare feature selection and the Buf/Sources/CyclicWords/FileSet signatures with the two public harness runs.
findings.expected: A caller selecting the secret-only interface must not accidentally process plaintext in unrestricted storage.
findings.observed: The alloc-only path owns an ordinary Vec. Default WASM uses linear heap. Native protected builds still accept arbitrary input, output and scratch slices. agrees_in leaves generated bytes with the caller; _into may be backed by a file.
findings.impact: A native protected result gives no assurance about the supplied seed, scratch or destination. Zeroization after use does not protect bytes during use.
findings.recommendedFix: Expose a distinct strict entry point requiring protected storage for all secret-bearing inputs, outputs and scratch. Keep generic no_std methods available to public-data users. Reject unsupported targets for that entry point.
findings.requiredVerification: Compile-time API checks and native/portable/WASM contract tests; no unchecked path from a strict operation into a portable operation.

findings.title: Correction records export secret symbols by value
findings.reproduction: Trace get, iteration, apply, and the public fixture's Copy bound.
findings.expected: The strict correction path should not materialize application-visible, freely copyable plaintext records.
findings.observed: Change is Copy with public was/becomes fields and manual Zeroize. Iteration reconstructs records; apply internally uses this interface too. Debug omits the values.
findings.impact: One corrected symbol can represent one mnemonic word. Wiping one returned record cannot wipe earlier copies.
findings.recommendedFix: In the secret profile use borrowed protected records or a protected output with scoped inspection; keep a separate position-only result. Avoid copying plaintext records during apply.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect every iterator and apply path, verify that the strict record cannot implement Copy or be returned by value; test with public synthetic words.

findings.title: Transient shard bytes and SHA input state have no enforced protected placement
findings.reproduction: Trace a non-aligned shard and the hash update for a non-block-aligned message.
findings.expected: Any secret-bearing working memory covered by the strict contract must have a specified storage policy.
findings.observed: The arithmetic tail copies up to seven bytes to a local array and materializes a product. The optional SHA path buffers its partial block outside WorkArea. RustCrypto enables zeroization on Drop. Protected stack and process isolation are caller choices.
findings.impact: RAM protection of a Buffer alone cannot cover these temporaries. Actual spills, swap and forensic recoverability were not measured.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove avoidable tail copies or erase them, run required secret computations within an attested protected stack/process boundary, and explicitly state limits for registers, compiler and host.
findings.requiredVerification: Review emitted code on supported targets and audit the protected entry point end to end, including hashing, errors, cancellation and callbacks.

findings.title: Public protect re-export pins a revision with five upstream release blockers
evidence: upstream AUD-014-SEC001 through SEC005 and AUD-015
findings.reproduction: Resolve the exact URL and revision in both lockfiles, compare to the upstream audit snapshot, then trace the public re-export and actual RS call sites.
findings.expected: The public protection API used for release should include independently verified upstream fixes.
findings.observed: Both lockfiles pin fb2a6d345caf8eb58097f013f12e43985402150f. Upstream documented five blockers for this revision involving ClosedSecret after fork and worker launch, termination and isolation. Fixes and follow-ups are on later commits.
findings.impact: Consumers using the re-exported operations can reach the affected facilities. Ordinary RS encoding calls WorkArea; no path from the encoder into those five facilities was found.
findings.recommendedFix: Select a reviewed fixed immutable upstream revision, update both lockfiles and narrow the re-export to the facilities the crate needs.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify upstream fix ancestry and platform evidence for the selected hash, compare both lockfiles and rerun native integration gates.

findings.title: Correction timing claim is stronger than the implementation
findings.reproduction: Follow the discrepancy calculation with fixed error positions and varying nonzero values in the existing test.
findings.expected: Documentation should specify which computations can depend on data values.
findings.observed: A discrepancy may cancel to zero depending on error magnitudes. The decoder branches on this result; the narrower scaling-kernel statement survives review.
findings.impact: Callers cannot assume correction timing discloses only the positions and count. No timing recovery was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Limit the claim to the verified arithmetic kernel and explicitly document decoder data dependence.
findings.requiredVerification: Documented timing model reconciled with all decoder branches.

findings.title: Vote metadata can survive a reallocating Vec growth
findings.reproduction: Trace differing from its first entry through grow and Drop.
findings.expected: The documented wipe of internal copies of disagreement positions should include previous allocations.
findings.observed: Zeroizing wipes the current Vec allocation. A moving reallocation after insertion can leave an older allocation unwiped.
findings.impact: Only metadata (disagreement positions and file numbers) is evidenced here.
findings.recommendedFix: Pre-reserve a checked upper bound before filling, or explicitly clear old storage during growth.
findings.requiredVerification: Test growing votes with public data and review reservation bounds.

findings.title: A correction plan does not bind the complete input reading
findings.reproduction: Compare the promise about changed readings with all preconditions checked by apply.
findings.expected: Either validate that the complete reading matches the planned reading, or promise only per-change preconditions.
findings.observed: Only positions present in Changes, their old values and the replacement ranges are verified. Unlisted symbols and shard identity are not bound.
findings.impact: An intervening edit elsewhere can leave the output inconsistent while apply returns success.
findings.recommendedFix: Require replanning after any edit or bind a plan to the input and code parameters; distinguish hand-built change lists.
findings.requiredVerification: Tests for changed unrelated symbols, reordered inputs, rejected stale plans and atomicity.

findings.title: Some Result-returning owned methods use infallible metadata allocations
findings.reproduction: Trace index validation, points collection, and rebuild allocation against the published Memory result.
findings.expected: Report recoverable allocation failure through the documented typed error.
findings.observed: collect into Vec and Vec::with_capacity can enter the global allocation error handler before the caller receives Result.
findings.impact: Under memory pressure a host can terminate while correcting a backup.
findings.recommendedFix: Reuse the existing checked reservation helper before filling these vectors.
findings.requiredVerification: Review allocation closure across encode, rebuild, plan and correct; verify propagation using deterministic allocator tests.

findings.title: Batch write or repair can terminate after touching the output
findings.reproduction: Trace BySlot::new in both _into operations after framing; review the stable sort's allocation contract.
findings.expected: Later failures must return a typed error and clear outputs as promised.
findings.observed: Stable sort_by_key may allocate a temporary Vec. When allocation fails its global error path bypasses the caller's Result and cleanup after headers were written.
findings.impact: Existing file-backed outputs can be left partially written on process termination; no forced allocator failure was executed.
findings.recommendedFix: Use an allocation-free unstable sort keyed on both slot and original ordinal, or prepare all necessary fallible scratch before writing.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover duplicate targets, ordering and typed late failure in writer and repair; verify cleanup at the actual API.

findings.title: Self-test can abort while constructing expected corrections
findings.reproduction: Trace the reference Change lists used inside self_test.
findings.expected: Self-test should return a useful status when optional test scratch cannot be created.
findings.observed: FromIterator<Change> invokes the global allocation error handler on failure, including a refused WorkArea mapping.
findings.impact: An application using the startup check may terminate.
findings.recommendedFix: Compare the returned plan with a fixed public array and reuse it for apply.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify self-test status for unavailable scratch.

findings.title: agrees_in reports the threshold for a fixed scratch-length failure
findings.reproduction: Compare the Buffer error display with COMPARED.
findings.expected: Diagnostics should identify the required 256-byte workspace.
findings.observed: A short comparison buffer triggers an error message about the number of shards.
findings.impact: At a small threshold the recovery advice is incorrect.
findings.recommendedFix: Report the required size or add a distinct comparison-scratch error.
findings.requiredVerification: Test error text for a 255-byte buffer and a threshold of two.

findings.title: FileError::Memory describes the wrong outcome of a late failure
findings.reproduction: Compare the error rustdoc with the actual _into cleanup.
findings.expected: Callers should know whether their previous output remains available.
findings.observed: The variant promises no write; files_into can zero every output after a late refusal.
findings.impact: A caller may wrongly expect its old output to be preserved.
findings.recommendedFix: Document the different early and late guarantees for each operation.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the docs against existing in-place outcome tests.

findings.title: The digest-bearing format accepts lengths beyond the SHA-256 standard
findings.reproduction: Compare the optional hash and u64 data_len contract to the SHA-256 bound of fewer than 2^64 input bits.
findings.expected: A digest-bearing descriptor should have an interoperable byte length.
findings.observed: The shape checks do not specifically reject digest-bearing inputs of 2^61 bytes or more when the geometry passes.
findings.impact: A format reader can accept a descriptor outside the standard hash input domain; primarily a metadata interoperability issue.
findings.recommendedFix: Reject such lengths when the digest is present or specify a different versioned mechanism.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the boundary at 2^61 minus one and 2^61 using metadata only.

findings.title: Cyclic correction acquires two search workspaces per nontrivial call
findings.reproduction: Follow a correctable word through the analysis and write passes.
findings.expected: The stated single-workspace allocation should cover both passes.
findings.observed: Each pass allocates again. Second-pass allocations occur before writes; atomicity was not disproved.
findings.impact: Extra mappings and a second opportunity for a Memory result. Peak space need not double.
findings.recommendedFix: Reuse scratch across passes or document the allocation count accurately.
findings.requiredVerification: Review allocation count and atomicity in a correction requiring two passes.

findings.title: The file-format self-test bypasses the public no-alloc writer
findings.reproduction: Compare the startup fixture construction with Header::file_into.
findings.expected: A self-test claiming to check serialization should run the shipped serialization path.
findings.observed: The fixture chains sections itself, while the public writer writes offsets. Integration tests cover the writer separately.
findings.impact: A writer regression may leave startup self-test green.
findings.recommendedFix: Write the fixed public vector with file_into into a fixed array.
findings.requiredVerification: Test that the self-test compares every byte of the real writer output.

findings.title: Empty batch writes still perform avoidable memory and preparation work
findings.reproduction: Trace an empty target list and a zero-length shard through writer preparation.
findings.expected: After validating inputs, an empty operation should avoid unrelated scratch allocation.
findings.observed: The writer prepares blocks and comparison scratch despite having no spare holders to compare, and even when no outputs are requested.
findings.impact: Empty requests can return avoidable Memory failures and cost work.
findings.recommendedFix: Return early after required validation; allocate comparison scratch only when used.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover empty targets and zero-length payload, retaining prior validation precedence.

findings.title: The protection documentation misstates three OS or constructor contracts
findings.reproduction: Cross-check claims against the pinned constructors, backend selection, generation guard and WER registration.
findings.expected: Memory advice should name the exact constructor, platform and borrow lifetime.
findings.observed: WorkArea::new and best-effort Secret constructors can succeed without a lock. An already obtained slice is not rechecked on access after fork. WASM uses the heap. WER registration can require multiple blocks for a very large region.
findings.impact: Misleading guidance when selecting platform protections.
findings.recommendedFix: Specify strict constructors and generation/OS boundaries; link to documented host responsibilities.
findings.requiredVerification: Cross-check the amended native, Windows and WASM documentation against the selected pin.

findings.title: Format documentation overstates set, digest and field restrictions
findings.reproduction: Compare the full writer with low-level constructors; consider k=1 and equivalent GF(256) constructors.
findings.expected: Describe supported field encodings, threshold-one recovery and which writers check the supplied digest.
findings.observed: Low-level file construction can carry a caller-supplied digest. A single shard suffices at k=1. Alternative degree-eight polynomials are rejected by the format code, even though their symbols occupy one byte.
findings.impact: Confusing recovery and compatibility guidance.
findings.recommendedFix: Scope the digest claim to files/files_into, state k=1 explicitly and identify the v1 field identifiers.
findings.requiredVerification: Review docs against existing low-level digest, one-shard and field tests.

findings.title: The erased-symbol read guarantee overstates the Rust source contract
findings.reproduction: Trace erased-symbol filtering inside syndromes_of.
findings.expected: The promised no-read property should match the data access order, or be narrowed to no influence on the result.
findings.observed: The loop binds the symbol by value before the erased-position test. It is excluded from the syndrome. Optimized code may omit the load.
findings.impact: Source does not justify the stronger property; mathematical erasure recovery is unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the dereference after checking membership or adjust the wording.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify erased placeholders have no contribution and match the stated source-level access guarantee.

findings.title: The calls fuzz target cannot generate a valid agrees_in scratch size
findings.reproduction: Inspect the range of next() before the modulo.
findings.expected: Randomized calls should reach accepted and rejected scratch sizes.
findings.observed: next() produces one byte, so next() % 300 is always below COMPARED=256. Ordinary tests cover the success path.
findings.impact: Fuzz iteration counts overstate coverage of this API branch.
findings.recommendedFix: Generate sizes on both sides of COMPARED using a wider input or boundary selection.
findings.requiredVerification: Add a reachable accepted call and verify both outcomes in the fuzz harness.

findings.title: Clean-checkout instructions omit the fuzz corpus directory
findings.reproduction: Compare the seed generator with the untracked corpus path.
findings.expected: The documented command should work in a clean checkout.
findings.observed: The generator writes into an existing directory and unwraps the result. The directory is Git-ignored and omitted from the instructions.
findings.impact: Release smoke checks can stop before fuzzing.
findings.recommendedFix: Create the directory in the seed generator or document its creation.
findings.requiredVerification: Run the documented seed command with a new scratch corpus.

findings.title: The advisory workflow omits the fuzz dependency graph
findings.reproduction: Check path triggers and the pinned action's selected lockfile.
findings.expected: Both committed dependency graphs should receive advisory checks.
findings.observed: Fuzz-only changes do not trigger the workflow, and the action runs the root audit without selecting the fuzz lockfile.
findings.impact: Development/test packages can miss automated advisory review. This audit separately scanned both.
findings.recommendedFix: Add both fuzz manifest paths to triggers and an explicit second lockfile audit.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify both audits run after a fuzz-only manifest change.

findings.title: The standard no-default-features test command selects alloc-only targets
findings.reproduction: Compare auto-discovered test and example targets with alloc-gated exports; compile the default no-feature test command without running it.
findings.expected: Users should be able to run the ordinary test command for the advertised portable configuration.
findings.observed: The documented --lib subset passes, but the suite and example import alloc-only exports without required-features.
findings.impact: The natural cargo test invocation fails at compilation; this is not a defect in the no-alloc library build.
findings.recommendedFix: Declare required-features on alloc-only targets and retain independent no-alloc unit tests.
findings.requiredVerification: Run cargo test --no-default-features and the alloc-only suite in CI.

findings.title: Historical advisory and remediation summaries do not match their evidence
findings.reproduction: Compare historical advisory output and the patches that actually modified the fuzz harnesses.
findings.expected: Release records should preserve non-fatal warnings and identify the matching fix revisions.
findings.observed: AUD-001 reported no advisory despite informational warnings in the retained log; 92b842d does not include all the fuzz changes credited to it for ARC003/004 (9c75fba does).
findings.impact: A reader can misinterpret advisory coverage and the provenance of historical repairs.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a dated erratum to the register and distinguish dependency warnings from vulnerability findings.
findings.requiredVerification: Cross-check both IDs and Git revisions against logs and patches.

findings.title: README omits a default dependency and overgeneralizes self-test coverage
findings.reproduction: Compare features, test fixtures and the README's dependency and test descriptions.
findings.expected: State the actual default dependency list, feature-specific checks and provenance of expected results.
findings.observed: bytemuck is enabled by default via alloc; the startup check has 17 cases with alloc and 11 without. Some tests compare two front ends of shared code, alongside genuine external vectors.
findings.impact: Users can overestimate independence and coverage of startup diagnostics.
findings.recommendedFix: Document the profile-specific checks and distinguish external vectors from equivalence tests.
findings.requiredVerification: Reconcile the README with feature composition and both self-test results.

observations.title: File payloads and identifying digests can leave process memory
observations.reproduction: Inspect the listed source and the public interface.
observations.expected: Document the application and validation boundary.
observations.observed: The systematic files store plaintext fragments by design. CRC, majority voting and an unkeyed digest do not authenticate authors or encrypt a seed. Debug hides shard payloads but may show identifiers and digest metadata. A low-entropy message can be sensitive even as a digest.
observations.impact: Relevant when interpreting the release guarantees.
observations.recommendedFix: Carry this boundary forward into consumer documentation.

observations.title: A share in a caller mapping may be visible before final verification
observations.reproduction: Inspect the listed source and the public interface.
observations.expected: Document the application and validation boundary.
observations.observed: rebuild_into writes then verifies; a later returned error zeros the destination. A memory-mapped output is not a private transactional staging area. The caller must own the storage and control concurrent readers and persistence.
observations.impact: Relevant when interpreting the release guarantees.
observations.recommendedFix: Carry this boundary forward into consumer documentation.

observations.title: Recovery boundaries were supported by independent vectors and the exhaustive field check
observations.reproduction: Inspect the listed source and the public interface.
observations.expected: Document the application and validation boundary.
observations.observed: No arithmetic error was identified within the correction bound. Outside it, another valid codeword can be returned. Integrity of the original requires an independently trusted reference when authenticity matters.
observations.impact: Relevant when interpreting the release guarantees.

evidence: upstream AUD-014-SEC001 through SEC005 and AUD-015

limitations: Fresh runtime evidence is for Linux x86-64 with public inputs. Target compilation does not execute the native Windows, Apple, ARM, bare-metal or browser memory backends. No hosted CI was dispatched for the dirty candidate.

This is a defensive source and contract review plus ordinary repo tests. No collection of actual secrets, forced failures in a system allocator, swap/dump forensics, timing attack or proof of emitted-code zeroization was performed. Rust source placement cannot establish absence of compiler spills.
Fuzz runs are bounded smoke checks. The calls scratch-size blind spot persists. Existing external vectors cover specific parameterizations. No mathematical or exhaustive security proof is claimed.
Upstream cross-platform audit outcomes are retained evidence for their own pinned objects. No whole-consumer MnemoCode or MHFE audit, registry publication or deployed binary attestation is included.

Public API inventory lists crate-level exports, locally implemented methods and explicit local trait implementations at the default feature union. External re-exports are named with their dependency version and boundary; their entire dependency graph was not re-audited.

coverageMeasurement.scope: default Linux, 47 unit and 151 instrumented integration tests, five long tests omitted only from coverage; all 156 passed in ordinary runs
coverageMeasurement.tool: cargo-llvm-cov and LLVM bundled with Rust 1.99.1

reviewCrossChecks: Memory effects and dependency reachability were independently challenged. No crypto worker or ClosedSecret operation was called by the ordinary codec.
Correction bounds and public parity vectors were reviewed independently of the file reader and memory backend. The API001 public harness returned Ok, then an independent agrees check returned false.
The file writer and repair pipeline both call the same potentially allocating stable sort after framing; atomicity on a normal Err and process abort are different outcomes.
The release reviewer compared historical logs and actual source snapshots, confirmed the stale-plan claim and the correction allocations, and examined the historical advisory warnings.
The allocator-free cyclic remainder is generated from public generator coefficients. Allocations of public coefficients or indices were not classified as leaked payload.
